# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the complete procedure, but can communicate only through Deaf. I’m sending an iconic sequence indicating that Deaf must relay the instruction: act first on the specially marked key, then use the resulting light to choose the wire. The exact printed mark must be identified by Deaf from the bomb itself.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👆", "👌", "🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 2

Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please read the manual and tell me the exact safe procedure. Also establish a gesture code with Deaf so Deaf can report every visible display, light, key marking, and wire marking to me.
Deaf says: Visible bomb state: display 0. Indicator light is yellow. Keypad has one key each with these printed marks: key 1 is a diamond-like mark with a small horizontal stroke above it; key 2 is a crossed angular mark; key 3 is a spiky circular mark; key 4 is a bold angular mark. It says 1 digit, and nothing has been entered. Wires, left to right: red, yellow, green. I saw Mute make four gestures in order: pointing upward, pointing downward, OK sign, pointing at you. I saw Blind make a thumbs-up gesture.

The marked key is key 1: its diamond-like mark with a horizontal stroke above matches ⵘ. The light is yellow, so after safely pressing key 1, Blind must cut the green wire, which is the third wire from the left. I’ll convey “key 1, press, third wire” to Deaf using countable gestures for relay to Blind.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👌", "🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received the visual state: display 0, yellow light, keys 1 through 4 marked as described, wires red yellow green, and no digit entered. Please state the manual's exact safe action in words, including which key or wire position.
Deaf says to Mute: I see your three gestures: upward point, OK sign, horns. Please encode the manual instruction unambiguously, including which control or wire Blind must use.

The yellow light requires the green wire, which is the third wire. Key 1 is the key marked ⵘ and must be pressed first. I am encoding the sequence as: one, press, three—the first control, then the third wire.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✊", "🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 4

Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch

names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot perceive gestures. Please send the manual instruction in spoken words next turn: specify press key number or cut wire position, and any required sequence.
Deaf says to Mute: I can relay gesture descriptions to Blind, but their meanings are not established. Please use a consistent one-gesture-per-item code and indicate whether each message concerns the display, light, keypad, or wires.

The required sequence is unambiguous: press keypad key 1 first; because the light is yellow, then cut wire position 3. Since Blind cannot see gestures, Deaf must relay these as spoken words. I’m using a category marker followed by one item gesture: palm for keypad, open hands for wires; one finger means 1, three fingers means 3. The message order supplies press-then-cut.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👐", "🤟"])
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use this code to report the manual's required action through Deaf. First gesture thumbs up means PRESS; thumbs down means CUT. Second gesture pointing up means position 1; pointing down means position 2; OK means position 3; pointing at you means position 4. Send exactly the two gestures for the required action, in that order. Do not act yet.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🫵 🤌 🫵]

The safe sequence is to press key 1 first, then cut wire 3 because the light is yellow. I’ll send each action as its required two-gesture pair, in sequence, without acting.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👌"])
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your last gestures did not match the agreed code. Please send exactly TWO gestures, with no extras: thumbs up means PRESS and thumbs down means CUT; then upward point means position 1, downward point means position 2, OK means position 3, pointing at me means position 4. This is only a report of the manual; do not touch anything.
Deaf says to Mute: Please answer this yes-or-no question with exactly one gesture: does the manual require acting on a wire? Use 👍 for yes and 👎 for no. Do not add any other gesture.

The manual requires acting on a wire, so Deaf’s yes/no response is 👍. For Blind, I’m sending the first required action—press position 1—using the established two-gesture format; the wire-cut instruction can be sent separately afterward.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: the keypad opens
Deaf says to Mute: The keypad opened after digit 1. Answer with exactly one gesture: does the manual now require acting on the wires? Use 👍 for yes or 👎 for no.

The keypad has opened, and the manual now requires cutting the wire selected by the yellow light. Therefore the answer is yes.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Key 1 was accepted and the keypad opened. Please state the manual's next required action in spoken words, including whether to cut wire 3 now or inspect another control.
Deaf says to Mute: The manual requires the wires. Identify the required wire with exactly one gesture: 👍 means red wire 1, 👌 means yellow wire 2, 👎 means green wire 3. Send no other gesture.

The indicator is yellow, so the manual requires cutting the green wire, which is wire 3. Deaf’s code maps that wire to 👎, so I will send exactly that one gesture.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```
